Chapter 8: Praying Through Crisis—Finding Strength in Difficult Seasons
Every family faces tough seasons. Maybe it's illness, loss, financial stress, or something completely unexpected. When those storms hit, even the strongest families can feel shaken. You might find yourself feeling helpless, overwhelmed, or just plain stuck. And honestly, that’s when prayer matters most—because it can turn from a daily habit into a real lifeline.
In the thick of crisis, prayer isn’t just about words—it’s about processing everything you’re feeling. Fear, grief, anger... you name it. Prayer gives you a safe space to lay it all out, even when you don’t have clear answers or any idea what tomorrow holds.
Here’s something to remember: You don’t have to hide your doubts or emotions. Bring your rawest feelings to God. Honesty in prayer isn’t just okay—it’s welcomed. No need to pretend you’re fine if you’re not.
So, how can you pray through a crisis? Let’s look at a few practical steps.
First, pray honestly. If you’re scared, angry, or confused, say it. Trust that you’re not being judged for what’s in your heart.
Next, ask for strength and wisdom. Instead of focusing only on what you want to happen, pray for resilience to keep going, wisdom to make the choices you’re facing, and peace to accept what can’t be changed.
And don’t go it alone. Invite others to pray with you. When you reach out to your community—friends, family, maybe even your faith group—you build a network of care and encouragement that can help you carry the weight.
Let me give you a real-world example. Imagine a parent whose child is seriously ill. There’s so much that’s out of their control, and that can be terrifying. But through prayer, that parent can find comfort, some clarity, and the strength to be present for their child—offering love, support, and hope, even when the outcome is uncertain.
Here’s the key takeaway: Crisis doesn’t mean you’ve failed. It’s actually an opportunity—a moment to grow deeper in faith, to draw your family closer, and to discover new sources of hope and strength you didn’t know you had. Prayer becomes the anchor that holds you steady when everything else feels adrift.
